spatial_claims.claim: Point C lies on segment AB, between A and B, cutting AB into segments AC and CB
AB is cut at C into two parts AC and CB (required for application of Prop 2.4)
AB is cut at C into two parts AC and CB (required for application of Prop 2.3)

configuration_map: The configuration is minimal: a single line segment AB with one interior point C dividing it into segments AC and CB. No auxiliary points are constructed. No triangles, circles, or angles are involved. The entire proof operates algebraically on area identities (squares and rectangles) derived from Props 2.3 and 2.4, both of which require only that C lies between A and B on line AB.
pass_reason: The proof is purely algebraic, making only the trivial spatial claim that C lies between A and B on segment AB. No geometric constructions, angle decompositions, interior/exterior claims, or ray orderings are present. The single spatial configuration is used consistently throughout all applications of Props 2.3 and 2.4. No contradictions are possible.
